topic.title: "Please write it down": the bank manager's insurance pitch
topic.claim: We don't say no to the person behind the desk because we assume they know better, and the only thing that breaks the spell is asking for it in writing.
topic.behaviour: Customers visit a branch for something routine and get steered toward ULIPs or insurance. One user got out of it by asking for the requirement in writing with an employee ID. Others say every bank does this.
topic.mechanism: We fear looking foolish in front of an authority, and branch targets turn a service desk into a sales desk. Many of us stay quiet to avoid friction.
topic.group: salaried urban Indians who bank at branches, and their parents
real_details: A user says a manager refused to process a pre-approved loan document unless they bought a ₹45,000 ULIP-insurance combo
The user asked for the demand in writing on letterhead to take to the ombudsman and the manager backed off
The user then saw an elderly man being pitched an endowment plan with his fixed deposit
Commenters said nearly all banks do this and one self-described bank employee said staff are pushed by targets
Another commenter described hearing a manager give staff targets on speakerphone
topic.why_now: The thread went viral and is a reminder before festival-season bonuses and FDs get parked in branches.

score.best_hook: I went to the bank to renew an FD. Twenty minutes later I was being sold a ULIP I never asked for.
